about.title: About this site
about.intro: This site shows how well each of the {capitals, number} EU capitals follows the 3-30-300 rule for urban greenery: three trees in view from every home, {canopy, number, percent} tree canopy around it and a park within a {distance, number, ::unit/meter} walk. Every capital is measured with the same open data and the same method.

basedOn.title: Based on
basedOn.text: The 3-30-300 rule comes from Cecil Konijnendijk, who set it out in the paper below, and a European study has assessed {cities, number} European cities against it. This site is based on both, but its method is its own: it looks at each building and each {cell, number, ::unit/meter} square, and its city limits and data differ, so its figures can differ from the European study.

papers.konijnendijk: Konijnendijk, C. C. (2023). Evidence-based guidelines for greener, healthier, more resilient neighbourhoods: Introducing the 3–30–300 rule. <journal>Journal of Forestry Research</journal> 34, 821–830.
papers.bertassello: Bertassello, L. E., van der Velde, M., Maes, J., Liu, S., Brandt, M. & Feyen, L. (2026). Assessing European cities with the 3-30-300 rule underscores the need for enhanced urban greening efforts. <journal>Nature Communications</journal> 17, 4846.
